description: Single, wages and interest: income-adjusted deduction partly phased out
Married, both 65+, large long-term gain: 44% gain deduction, $15,000 age-65 deduction each, phased income-adjusted deduction
working: SC1040 (2026): federal AGI = 60,000 + 5,000 + 8,000 + 51,000 = 124,000. Subtractions: 44% net capital gain deduction 0.44 x 51,000 = 22,440 (qualified dividends get no deduction); age-65 deduction 15,000 x 2 = 30,000 (no retirement deduction claimed). SC Income Adjusted Deduction (joint) 30,000 reduced by (124,000 - 80,000) / 110,000 = 0.4 -> 12,000 -> 18,000. Taxable = 124,000 - 22,440 - 30,000 - 18,000 = 53,560. Tax = 5.21% x 53,560 - 966 = 2,790.48 - 966 = 1,824.48 (= 597 + 5.21% x 23,560 = 1,227.48). (Federal: standard 32,200 + 2 x 1,650 = 35,500, senior deduction 2 x 6,000 = 12,000; taxable 76,500, of which 59,000 gains/qualified dividends at 0% (ordinary 17,500 + 59,000 under 98,900); tax 10% x 17,500 = 1,750.)
